saying: Most commenters told FDA to keep synthetic and real-world results separate, and to pool benchmarking with clinical confirmation only if sampling frames are shown exchangeable, with confirmation governing acceptance. They also asked for disaggregated subgroup, scenario and failure-mode reporting instead of single pooled scores, prespecified estimands and precision, and repeated-run variance reporting to handle nondeterministic outputs.

disagreement.text: Commenters split on whether synthetic data may ever contribute to a performance estimate: some would permit combining after documented transportability, weighting and provenance, while others say synthetic data provides no valid denominator, no validated adequacy method exists, and it should be limited to failure-finding and rare-event coverage.

sides.summary: Combining synthetic and real evidence is acceptable when transportability, provenance and distributional differences are documented.
Synthetic data must never establish performance rates; it lacks a real-population denominator and no validated adequacy method exists.
